headline: Leclerc holds off Russell by 0.427s in Silverstone
standfirst: Charles Leclerc won the British Grand Prix for Ferrari, finishing 0.427s ahead of George Russell, with Lewis Hamilton completing the podium after 52 laps of Silverstone.

sections.title: The start
sections.body: Kimi Antonelli lined up first on the grid. Leclerc got the better launch and led the field across the line at the end of the opening lap. The biggest winner of the opening lap was Ocon, up 6 places to 11th.

sections.title: How it unfolded
sections.body: The lead changed hands 2 times. Laps led: Leclerc (42) and Antonelli (10). Leclerc took the lead for good on lap 36. The race was neutralised by 2 safety car periods (lap 48–51, 51–52).

sections.title: Strategy
sections.body: Leclerc made 2 stops, running medium → hard → soft tyres. The field made 51 pit stops in total; the quickest stationary time was 2.3s for Bortoleto on lap 26.

sections.title: Movers
sections.body: Franco Colapinto made up the most ground, climbing 10 places from 19th to 9th. Antonelli went the other way, slipping from 1st to 15th. Timing recorded 232 on-track position changes, 19 of them by Sainz.

sections.title: Retirements
sections.body: Verstappen (lap 47), Albon (lap 44) and Hulkenberg (lap 37) failed to finish.

sections.title: Conditions and pace
sections.body: It stayed dry throughout. Track temperature ranged from 38°C to 44°C, with air at 24–26°C. Kimi Antonelli set the fastest lap, a 1:31.777 on lap 37.
